_doc: Named residents of Thornfield (docs/design/FOUNDATION_PLAN.md F8). Source of truth for scripts/world/thornfield/roster.gd and tools/thornfield/gen_dialogue.py (dialogue/thornfield/<id>.json). job = WorldSim job index (0 farmer, 1 blacksmith, 2 merchant, 3 guard, 4 laborer, 5 woodcutter). home/work are building ids from SliceTown (thornfield_house_N, thornfield_smithy, ...) or site ids (thornfield_brewery, thornfield_farm, thornfield_mill, thornfield_barn). schedule overrides {from, to, phase} replace the baseline schedule phase (home work market inn temple train social) for hours in [from, to). bind=false people are not WorldSim rows (Hesta stands at the brewery as a station).

greeting: First pint is free if you can name the hop.
rumour: The tithe barn is half full. Half. After a good harvest.

opinions.odo_marsh: Odo has the best nose in the vale and the worst temper.
opinions.wilm_garrow: Wilm drinks more than he pays for. I keep a tab. He keeps promises about it.
opinions.reeve_alden: Alden counts barley the way I count grudges: carefully, and aloud.

greeting: Mind the kettles. They bite.
Morning. If it smells good, it is mine; if it smells wrong, it is Pell's.
rumour: Someone has been in the cellar. The kegs are one short and I counted twice.
Hesta tastes every batch. I taste it first and pretend I did not.

opinions.pell_hargrove: Pell malts well and talks too much. Mostly in that order.
opinions.hesta_thorne: Hesta pays late and pays fair. I have worked for worse.
opinions.joss_brannock: Joss waters his ale. I will say no more.

greeting: Smell that? That is next week's ale, sprouting.
Ho! Mind the damp floor, it is the whole secret.
rumour: I swear there was a light in the tithe barn last night. No one has a key but the reeve and Hesta.
Barley comes in sound and goes bad on top. Rot does not work like that.

opinions.wilm_garrow: Wilm is my cousin. I love him. I would not leave him alone with a full barrel.
opinions.odo_marsh: Odo is all bark. Mostly. The kettles, though, those bite.

greeting: Fine weather for barley, if the wolves let it be.
Mind the furrows, friend.
rumour: Tracks by the hedge again this morning. Big ones. They are testing it.
The thorn hedge holds, but not forever. Nothing does.

opinions.tilda_fenn: My sister works harder than any two men and would box my ears for saying it.
opinions.cobb_ardley: Cobb says the winter will be hard. Cobb says that every year. He is right one year in three.

greeting: If you are lost, the road is the long straight thing.
Hello. Do not step on the seedlings.
rumour: Wolves took a ewe from the high pen. Left the bell, took the ewe.
I counted sacks twice. The barn is short and nobody will say why.

opinions.bram_oakley: My brother thinks every shadow is a wolf. Tonight it might be.

greeting: Hmph. Young legs. Use them.
Weather is turning. My knee says so.
rumour: I have seen three wolf winters. This feels like the fourth.
The old stones hum less than they did.

opinions.old_hild: Hild remembers when the hedge was a seedling. She will tell you, too.
opinions.bram_oakley: Bram is a good lad. Too loud, but good.

greeting: Hello! Have you been to Kingsreach? Is it as big as they say?
Morning. Is it just me, or is the sky bigger today?
rumour: The pigs were restless last night. Pigs know.
Someone left the wicket open at the sheep pen. Not one of us.

opinions.edric_vane: Edric sells good rope and bad advice.

greeting: If it is not broken do not bring it. If it is, leave it.
Heat is good. Hammers are better.
rumour: Three sets of wolf-bells, a dozen nails, and a hinge for the barn door. It had been forced, that hinge.
Iron prices are up. Nobody tells the Council.

opinions.tam_birch: Young Tam wants a good sword. He needs a good sleep first.
opinions.edric_vane: Edric undercuts me on nails. I forgive him. Mostly.

greeting: Bread's still warm, love. Take a heel.
The oven wakes me before the cock does.
rumour: Pell's wife says he comes home smelling of the barn, not the malt-house.
Half the village owes me for bread, and Wilm owes me twice.

opinions.wilm_garrow: Wilm Garrow eats my bread and tells me it is the best in the vale. Pays in compliments.
opinions.joss_brannock: Joss buys flour from me and sells stew to everyone else. I do not mind.

greeting: Welcome, welcome. Rope, lamp oil, boots, anything under the sun.
Need something? Probably I have it.
rumour: Wilm Garrow bought lamp oil twice this week and has no lamp that I know of.
A trader said the roads east are bad. Prices will follow.

opinions.roderic_hale: Roderic's nails are fine nails. Mine are cheaper.
opinions.wilm_garrow: Wilm owes me forty coppers and a very good story.

greeting: Come in, come in. The stew is hot and the beds are only a little damp.
A seat by the fire for a friendly face.
rumour: A traveller asked about the barn today. Offered to pay for the answer. I sent him away.
Guards drink for free on Fridays. Somebody has to keep the peace.

opinions.odo_marsh: Odo thinks I water my ale. I merely stretch it. There is a difference.
opinions.hesta_thorne: Hesta's ale outsells mine three to one. We toast to her anyway.

greeting: Keep your blade sheathed inside the walls and we will get on.
Captain Ashdown. State your business.
rumour: Tracks of five or six wolves by the north hedge. A pack with a plan.
I put Ines on the barn road at night. Somebody has been prowling.

opinions.ines_carrow: Carrow is the best I have. She does not know it.
opinions.tam_birch: Birch is green. He will learn or the wolves will teach him.

greeting: Evening. Keep to the lit roads.
Night watch. Say your business.
rumour: I saw a shape slip into the tithe barn two nights ago. By the time I reached it, nothing.
Wolves at the hedge, three nights in a row.

opinions.wulf_ashdown: The Captain does not sleep. I think he is made of oak.
opinions.tam_birch: Tam talks on watch. I let him, it keeps him awake.

greeting: Halt! ...Sorry. Habit. Good day.
Nothing to report, sir. Ma'am. Whoever you are.
rumour: I heard howling from the forest last night. It sounded close. It sounded organised.
Roderic is making me a proper sword. Eventually.

opinions.roderic_hale: Master Hale says I swing like I am chasing flies.

greeting: Grind and bear it, as they say. Welcome to the mill.
Flour in the hair, flour in the soul.
rumour: Sound barley is getting scarce. What I am sent lately is half mould.
The sails turned by themselves last night. Wind, I said. Wind.

opinions.hesta_thorne: Hesta's barley is the best in the vale. When it arrives.
opinions.bram_oakley: Bram brings wheat and fears. I take both.

greeting: Cough? Rash? Heartbreak? I have a tea for all three.
Sit. You look pale. Everyone looks pale.
rumour: Wilm Garrow has been buying poppy and moulds. Odd combination for a man who claims to sleep well.
Mould on barley is not rot. Rot smells earthy. This smelled of sweet vinegar. Someone poured it.

opinions.old_hild: Hild has outlived three healers and she will outlive me.
opinions.wilm_garrow: Wilm is troubled. I would help him if he let me.

greeting: Are you a hero? You look like a hero.
Want to see a frog? I have a frog.
rumour: Pip says the barn is haunted. I say it is a person. Pip says that is worse.
Wolves are just big dogs. Mama says they are not. Mama is wrong, I think.

opinions.pip_oakley: Pip is my best friend. Mostly. We argue about dragons.
opinions.wren_fenn: Wren is too little to play knights. She can be the dragon.

greeting: ...Hello.
I know where the cats sleep. Do you want to know?
rumour: I saw a man at the barn at night through my window. He carried a bucket.
I am not allowed to talk about it. Da says.

opinions.dilly_pennick: Dilly is loud. But she shares her bread.

greeting: Hi! I am Wren and I am seven!
Do you have a dog? I want a dog.
rumour: There is a big dog by the barn. He does not bark.
Mama says do not wander, but I wander a little.

opinions.dilly_pennick: Dilly lets me be the dragon. I am a very good dragon.

greeting: Sit by me, child. My legs have opinions.
I knew your grandmother. Or someone like her.
rumour: The hedge was my father's idea. He cursed it every winter and wept when he died.
There was a drifter once, years ago. Wilm's father. He also loved a barn at night.

opinions.granfer_aldous: Aldous is a fool. I have loved him for fifty years.
opinions.agnes_thistle: Agnes has good hands. She will not admit it.

greeting: Eh? Speak up, young one. Or do not, I will nod either way.
Sit. Have you heard the one about the three-legged ox?
rumour: Wolves came through the east pass in my youth. We lit bonfires and sang. Never saw one again.
Do not trust a man who is too friendly to a dog.

opinions.old_hild: Hild and I were nearly married. She says nearly. I say nearly.

residents.name: Wilm Garrow

greeting: Well, well. A friendly face. Spare a coin for a man between fortunes?
Evening. Lovely night for it.
rumour: Rot gets into every barn eventually. Nothing a man can do.
I was never near the barn. Ask anyone.

opinions.pell_hargrove: Pell is my cousin. Good lad. Does not ask questions.
opinions.hesta_thorne: Hesta is a hard woman. A fair one, I will say that.
opinions.edric_vane: Edric thinks I owe him. I think he owes me patience.

residents.secret: Paid by a Kingsreach grain factor to spoil Thornfield's tithe barley so the price would rise.

greeting: Reeve Cray. Whatever it is, it is in writing or it did not happen.
Mind the ledger on the way out.
rumour: The tithe barn count is short by eleven sacks. Eleven. I wrote it in ink.
Kingsreach wants its barley on time and bad news late.

opinions.hesta_thorne: Hesta and I do not agree. Which is why we get things done.
opinions.wulf_ashdown: Ashdown keeps the walls. I keep the books. Between us, the village stands.

greeting: Mm.
Careful where you walk. The forest bites.
rumour: There is a den north-east, past the old birches. Smells of wolf for a quarter-mile.
I have never seen so many tracks. They are not hunting, they are looking.

opinions.bram_oakley: Bram thinks wolves are demons. They are just hungry. Sometimes that is worse.

greeting: Peace be on you, traveller.
The bell tolls for those who listen.
rumour: People confess more at the barn door than at the altar, lately.
Wilm Garrow lit a candle at the shrine last night. He did not say for whom.

opinions.agnes_thistle: Agnes and I share the village's aches. She treats the bodies, I the rest.
